title.en: Buoyancy as weight of displaced fluid

summary: Apply a buoyant force from displaced volume rather than painting a water line, and keep that hydrostatic shortcut distinct from flow or stability.
objective: Compare the equilibrium draft of a sealed freely floating body with the initial upward or downward acceleration of a body released in still liquid.
applies_when: A body is placed in a still liquid and the question is whether it floats, sinks or hovers.
Draft, load line or ballast is used to explain displacement, not free-surface waves.
intent_signals: why does the boat sit lower when loaded
float a cork and sink a stone
example_prompts: Float a sealed hull and a solid block of the same mass in a tank and compare draft.
Let me change object density and see the submerged fraction follow the density ratio.
negative_signals: Wavy water shaders with no displaced volume.
Metacentric ship-stability claims from a single upward arrow.
not_for: Free-surface CFD, sloshing or planing hydrodynamics.
Rotational stability or metacentre, which the cited section does not cover.

principles: Buoyancy equals displaced-fluid weight. The density-ratio submerged fraction describes free floating equilibrium, not every transient pose.
Use sealed, nonflooding displacement geometry, finite positive volume and fluid density, and no external floor or tether support in the equilibrium comparison.
This model fixes orientation and vertical alignment; it does not infer rotational stability from an arbitrary force application point.
implementation: Own mass, sealed displacement volume, fluid density, water level and a monotone displaced-volume function of draft. Keep body density derived from mass/volume.

For quasi-static floating with 0<m<rho_fluid V_total, solve rho_fluid V_displaced=m over the admissible draft interval. At neutral density a fully submerged body has no uniquely selected depth. If heavier, report no free floating equilibrium rather than clamp to a false draft.

An optional transient vertical branch owns velocity and applies F=rho_fluid V_displaced g-m g. Apply force through the center of mass with rotation constrained. It does not promise convergence; any added drag is an explicitly authored dissipative model, not an Archimedes calibration.
Show equilibrium and transient readouts separately. Pause preserves velocity and time; reset restores initial pose, velocity, fluid level, mass and volume.
observable_checks: At the solved freely floating equilibrium, V_displaced/V_total equals mean object density/fluid density within tolerance.
A fully submerged heavier body released from rest initially accelerates downward. An upward-moving heavy body may continue upward briefly while decelerating.
Changing appearance alone leaves mass and displacement unchanged. Do not reject undamped transient bobbing merely because it has not settled.

creative_affordances: Cutaway hulls, ballast tanks and load-line marks make displacement legible.
Stylised boats may still use the same density-ratio check if they claim to float.
known_limits: The cited Archimedes section is static buoyancy in fluid at rest; metacentre and wave-making are not covered.
Overlap-volume estimators miss concavities, trapped air and free-surface setup unless modelled.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: The buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid. With gravity and buoyancy as the only vertical forces, their imbalance determines vertical acceleration; released from rest the body initially rises or sinks accordingly. At freely floating equilibrium the submerged-volume fraction equals mean object density divided by fluid density.
claims.scope: Still constant-density liquid, sealed nonflooding displacement, no floor or tether support; equilibrium fraction is separate from transients and excludes rotational stability.

source_refs.locator: 14.4, Archimedes' Principle; release-from-rest passage; Density and Archimedes' Principle
